misconception_description: Student believes that values must be explicitly converted to their current type to ensure type safety.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungPasanganTidakSama
kamus
  a, b, c, jumlah : integer
algoritma
  input(a, b, c)
  a <- integer(a)
  b <- integer(b)
  c <- integer(c)
  jumlah <- integer(0)
  if integer(a) != integer(b) then
    jumlah <- integer(jumlah) + 1
  endif
  if integer(a) != integer(c) then
    jumlah <- integer(jumlah) + 1
  endif
  if integer(b) != integer(c) then
    jumlah <- integer(jumlah) + 1
  endif
  output(integer(jumlah))
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student unnecessarily converts values to int throughout the code to ensure "type safety". This includes converting 0 to int(0), converting loop indices i to int(i), converting array elements arr[i] and arr[j] to int() when comparing them, converting the increment value 1 to int(1), and converting the return value cnt to int(cnt). Despite being redundant, these conversions don't break the code since the values are already integers - the program still functions correctly but with unnecessary overhead.
